title: Mike's Painting & Pressure Washing Alternative
description: Comparing Mike's Painting & Pressure Washing with Precision Paint Experts? Learn how washing, mildew treatment, and dry time belong in a painting scope.
h1: Mike's Painting & Pressure Washing vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: In a humid climate, the wash before the paint counts just as much as the coating. Here's a way to grade the cleaning and mildew steps in any painting proposal.

sections.h2: Comparing the cleaning step, not just the painting
body: If Mike's Painting & Pressure Washing is among the contractors you've asked to bid, you'll want to compare more than the paint. Other businesses aren't our subject here, so we won't describe them. Instead, this page focuses on the part of a quote people tend to skim: cleaning the surface, killing the mildew, and letting everything dry before the first coat.

Dark growth on the shady side of a house, a film of pollen on the trim, and chalky old paint all stop new paint from gripping. Washing is not a courtesy step; it is the foundation for everything that follows.

High pressure is useful on concrete and some masonry, but it can force water into siding joints and damage soft wood or older stucco. Soft washing uses lower pressure with cleaning solutions to remove growth without that risk. We offer both methods under our pressure washing and soft washing service and pick one surface by surface.
Noticing black streaks or fuzzy spots? Read our guide to mold and mildew on siding to learn what that growth is and why a plain rinse never keeps it away.

Concrete is a different story. Driveways, sidewalks, and the pool deck generally tolerate more pressure, and washing them along with the house leaves the whole lot looking done when the crew packs up. If you want those surfaces included, have them named on the quote so the scope is never in question.

sections.h2: What a solid prep scope says about washing
body: Whoever you hire, the estimate should answer these points in writing:
bullets: Which surfaces are washed, and by what method.
Whether a mildew treatment is applied, not only a rinse.
How long surfaces dry before primer or paint.
How plants, screens, and outlets are protected during washing.
What happens to loose paint exposed by the wash: scraping, sanding, spot-priming.

sections.h2: Where washing fits in our process
body: With us, the order is: walkthrough, then a written estimate, then prep days, then painting, then a final punch list that you sign. Washing kicks off those prep days, and after it come mildew treatment, scraping, sanding, setting nail pops, carpentry on rotted fascia, re-caulking, and spot-priming. Most full exteriors take three to seven working days with the wash and drying time on top, and our written schedule shows that time openly.

While walking the property, our crew lead uses a moisture meter anywhere a board or wall feels damp, since coating a wet surface ranks among the leading reasons paint lets go. To understand why, see humidity and peeling paint.

There's no charge and no commitment for an estimate, and it typically reaches you a business day after we visit. Once the house is clean and dry, siding and trim get premium 100% acrylic, and exterior work is covered by our written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years. Book a walkthrough or read about exterior painting in more detail.

faqs.q: Does your exterior quote include washing the house?
faqs.a: Yes. On every exterior repaint, washing and mildew treatment are built into the prep days, and the quote names the method and each surface.

faqs.q: Can I book soft washing without painting?
faqs.a: Yes. We do pressure washing and soft washing as their own jobs, not only as the first step before paint.

faqs.q: I rinsed off the mildew, so why is it back already?
faqs.a: A rinse clears what you can see, but the growth itself often survives. That's why our prep includes a mildew treatment before anything is painted.
